A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. All pages, including appendices, equations, algorithms, tables and figures, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched between versions.

before.justification: v3 reports original Othello and Chess evaluations, including confidence–accuracy relationships, conditioning-set ablations, attention-head pruning and train–test distribution analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical evaluations. Although the pretrained models originate from cited work, the paper reports its own analyses and experimental outcomes.

M1.justification: The attention-to-covariance transformation, recursive causal discovery, per-head processing and entropy-based confidence score remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 retain the same steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Othello and Chess environments, pretrained on real-world games and evaluated on randomly sampled legal-move sequences. Moving the Chess example into the main text adds no coverage.

E2.justification: The matched experiments retain the same comparison configurations: marginal, restricted and unrestricted conditioning tests, and opposite confidence-based head-pruning orders. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,000 test sequences, the 10,000-sample exception for short Chess sequences, the same evaluated sequence lengths, partial-correlation testing with alpha = 0.01, and the same pruning thresholds. No evaluation procedure or metric changes.

E4.justification: The conditioning-set ablation, attention-head pruning analysis, confidence–legality analysis, n-gram distribution comparison and illustrative recovered causal graphs are all retained. Their relocation and reformatting add no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals from an unpaired t-test for the conditioning-set ablation. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched plots retain their results despite renumbering and rearrangement. Both versions report 95% average Othello legal-move accuracy and 88% for 15-move inputs, with unchanged ablation, pruning, confidence–accuracy and n-gram findings.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 narrows the condition accompanying Equation 9 from hidden nodes generally to hidden confounders. Appendix B in v4 also explicitly characterizes ICD-Sep conditions as sufficient for soundness and completeness, replacing v3's compliance-required wording. The displayed equations and derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a causal interpretation of GPT attention, zero-shot causal structure learning, a confidence score, and its relationship to legal-move generation. Rewriting does not materially alter these core claims.

C2.justification: The mechanism discussion in Section 4.1 and the corresponding illustration now specifically qualifies the hidden-node omission statement using hidden confounders. This modestly narrows that interpretation. Explanations of the experimental findings, memorization caveats and proposed relevance to hallucination detection remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 of v4 newly identifies and links the Causality Lab repository used for causal discovery implementation and empirical evaluation. v3 has no equivalent implementation-access pointer; the documented experimental settings are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior world-model studies, ABCD and ICD remain unchanged. Related-work prose and reference layout are edited without adding or removing research contributions from the discussion.

P1.justification: v4 extensively copyedits the abstract, main sections, captions and appendices, correcting grammar and restructuring explanations. It also incorporates the former notation appendix into the main preliminaries and reorganizes the remaining appendices.

P2.justification: The Chess illustration and notation table move from the appendix into the main text. The six pruning panels change from one narrow row in v3 Figure 4 to a larger two-by-three arrangement in v4 Figure 5, and Figure 8 moves beside its appendix discussion. These substantially revise presentation while retaining the displayed evidence.

improvement.justification: v4 improves readability and access to the existing work through extensive copyediting, better placement of notation and examples, larger pruning plots, and an implementation repository pointer. These provide a supported usability and transparency gain. The empirical evidence and main theoretical argument are essentially retained, so the overall improvement is limited.
